name: auth-clerk-jwt
title: Auth — Clerk sessions (bring your own auth)
description: Use Clerk as the identity provider and let Clerk own the session: verify each request's Clerk session token against your instance's JWKS and feed the user, active organization, role and permissions into ctx.auth / RLS via a resolveIdentity adapter. For Clerk as a login button on a Lunora-owned better-auth session, use auth-clerk instead.
docs: Pass `clerkIdentity(env)` as `resolveIdentity` in your Worker entry (`createWorker({ resolveIdentity: clerkIdentity(env), … })`, or `.extend((env) => ({ resolveIdentity: clerkIdentity(env) }))` on the generated app builder). On the client, create the LunoraClient with `authTokenOnUpgrade: true` and call `setAuthTokenProvider(client, () => getToken(), { subject: userId })` from `lunorash/client` (`@lunora/client` without the umbrella) once signed in. Guide: https://lunora.sh/docs/concepts/external-auth

envVars.name: CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY
envVars.description: Your Clerk publishable key (pk_test_… / pk_live_…). Not a secret — the same key the frontend uses; it encodes the Frontend API that issues session tokens.

envVars.name: CLERK_AUTHORIZED_PARTIES
envVars.description: Required. Comma-separated origins of your frontend (checked against the token's azp claim), e.g. http://localhost:5173,https://app.example.com. An empty value stops the Worker at startup.
